Should I use the boiling water method or Ammonia fermentation to make dye out of mixed Hypogymnia lichen?

message.content: You can try the boiling water method to extract dye from mixed Hypogymnia lichen. This method involves boiling the lichen in water, allowing the dye to leach out into the water. Once the water cools, you can strain out the lichen and use the dyed water to color fabric or other materials.
The boiling water method can be used to make dye out of mixed Hypogymnia lichen. However, ammonia fermentation may be a better choice as it results in a deeper and more vibrant color.

Hypogymnia is a type of lichen that can be used to create a dye. The boiling water method involves boiling the lichen in water to extract the dye, while the ammonia fermentation method involves fermenting the lichen with ammonia to create a dye. Both methods have their pros and cons, so it is up to personal preference which one to use.

I would suggest using the boiling water method to make dye out of mixed Hypogymnia lichen. Boiling water is a simple and effective method that can help extract the dye from the lichen without the need for additional chemicals like ammonia. Additionally, boiling water is a safer option as it does not produce harmful fumes or waste products.
You should use the boiling water method.
